It was one of the first companies to successfully bring a comprehensive AI platform to the audit profession, effectively “pioneering the application of ensemble artificial intelligence to financial auditing”[[4]](https://www.v7labs.com/blog/ai-auditing-software-for-accountants-guide#:~:text=). This head start, combined with continuous innovation, has given MindBridge a strong reputation in the industry. Independent evaluations have described MindBridge as “the global leader in AI-powered financial risk discovery and anomaly detection”, highlighting how it helps professionals identify and analyze risk across broad datasets[[27]](https://www.mindbridge.ai/#:~:text=MindBridge%20,risk%20across%20broad%20financial%20datasets). Since its founding, MindBridge has accumulated a number of accolades that reflect its position: for instance, it was named a Gartner “Cool Vendor” in Finance in 2022[[28]](https://www.mindbridge.ai/company/#:~:text=MindBridge%20named%20a), and it has appeared in Gartner’s 2024 Hype Cycle report for emerging autonomous accounting technologies[[29]](https://www.mindbridge.ai/company/#:~:text=According%20to%20Gartner%C2%AE%2C%20%E2%80%9CA%20new,%E2%80%9D). It also earned a spot on Deloitte’s “Companies-to-Watch” list early on and more recently made the 2024 Deloitte Fast 500 as one of North America’s fastest-growing tech companies[[30]](https://www.mindbridge.ai/news/mindbridge-named-one-of-the-fastest-growing-technology-companies-in-north-america/#:~:text=MindBridge%20Named%20One%20of%20the,assessment%20in%20finance%20and%20auditing). These honors underscore MindBridge’s status as a leading innovator in audit tech.

items.quote: the most likely candidate magnetoreceptor of the light-dependent magnetic compass in birds
items.paragraph: - Cryptochrome 4a (Cry4a): Location: Cryptochrome 4 was more recently identified in birds and is present in the retina. Cry4a is the originally characterized isoform. In European robins and other birds, Cry4a protein is found in the long-wavelength-sensitive cones (the red-sensitive single cones) and in the double cone photoreceptors[[34]](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-020-72579-2?error=cookies_not_supported&code=b3ba2ed1-0f82-45d0-a502-b89a50d92c0a#:~:text=segments%2C%20the%20ganglion%20cell%20layer,documented%20magnetic). These cone types are fewer in number than UV cones, but double cones and LWS cones are sensitive to longer wavelengths (green/red) and contain pigmented oil droplets (which could filter some blue light). Function: Cry4a has emerged as another strong candidate for magnetoreception. Evidence supporting Cry4a’s role includes: (a) Cry4 (gene/protein) expression in the retina does not exhibit a strong circadian rhythm – it remains at fairly constant levels day and night[[35]](https://www.sciencealert.com/birds-see-magnetic-fields-cryptochrome-cry4-photoreceptor-2018#:~:text=The%20Lund%20team%20measured%20gene,reception%20over%20the%20circadian%20day)[[31]](https://www.sciencealert.com/birds-see-magnetic-fields-cryptochrome-cry4-photoreceptor-2018#:~:text=This%20finding%20was%20supported%20by,which%20found%20the%20same%20thing), unlike Cry1 or Cry2 which oscillate. A true magnetoreceptor should ideally be continuously available, so this steady expression is a positive sign. (b) In night-migratory birds like robins, Cry4 levels increase during the migratory season, when magnetic orientation is crucial, whereas non-migratory species (or non-migratory seasons) show lower expression[[36]](https://www.sciencealert.com/birds-see-magnetic-fields-cryptochrome-cry4-photoreceptor-2018#:~:text=Cry4%20is%20clustered%20in%20a,dependent%20magnetoreception). (c) Biochemical studies show that Cry4 can bind the FAD cofactor in a stable manner[[37]](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-020-72579-2?error=cookies_not_supported&code=b3ba2ed1-0f82-45d0-a502-b89a50d92c0a#:~:text=is%20Cry4%20of%20night,of%20the%20European%20robin50%2C%20and), and recent in vitro experiments demonstrated magnetic-field effects on the photochemistry of robin Cry4 (i.e. a radical-pair reaction in Cry4 can be influenced by weak magnetic fields)[[38]](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-020-72579-2?error=cookies_not_supported&code=b3ba2ed1-0f82-45d0-a502-b89a50d92c0a#:~:text=sense1%20%2C%2081%2C57%20%2C%2083%2C59,has%20been%20suggested%20to%20interact). (d) Cry4a is found in photoreceptor cells (cones) that receive ample light, and there are indications it might interact with the visual pigment in those cones (iodopsin) to modulate vision in a magnetically sensitive way[[37]](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-020-72579-2?error=cookies_not_supported&code=b3ba2ed1-0f82-45d0-a502-b89a50d92c0a#:~:text=is%20Cry4%20of%20night,of%20the%20European%20robin50%2C%20and). All these observations suggest Cry4a could serve as a magnetoreceptor or part of the magnetic sensing pathway. Some researchers have gone so far as to conclude Cry4 is “the most likely candidate magnetoreceptor of the light-dependent magnetic compass in birds” based on these data[[35]](https://www.sciencealert.com/birds-see-magnetic-fields-cryptochrome-cry4-photoreceptor-2018#:~:text=The%20Lund%20team%20measured%20gene,reception%20over%20the%20circadian%20day)[[39]](https://www.sciencealert.com/birds-see-magnetic-fields-cryptochrome-cry4-photoreceptor-2018#:~:text=But%20they%20made%20a%20couple,dependent%20magnetoreception). Nonetheless, Cry4’s role is considered complementary to Cry1a’s role – ongoing research is examining whether one or both are required.

items.quote: entail serious health risks for employees
items.paragraph: - Bias, Fairness, and Ethical Use: Generative AI systems can inadvertently introduce or amplify biases in workplace decisions, which is a significant challenge to equitable employment. If an AI tool is used in hiring or evaluations (even indirectly, e.g. an AI grades a writing test), any bias in its training data could lead to unfair outcomes (such as favoring certain demographics). Researchers have flagged that AI adoption could “entail serious health risks for employees” in a broad sense – including psychological stress from algorithmic management or unfair treatment[[54]](https://www.ilo.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/ILO_Safeday25_Report_EN_r8%2B%281%29.pdf#:~:text=Organization%20www,cancer%2C%20lung%20diseases%20and)[[55]](https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Estimation-results-increasing-requirements-regarding-workplace-flexibility_tbl3_360365774#:~:text=,). Ensuring AI fairness and avoiding discrimination is both an ethical and a legal imperative. This means companies must audit AI outputs for biased content (e.g. stereotyped language or lower-quality responses for certain groups) and include diverse perspectives in AI development. Another ethical challenge is maintaining human agency – workers should have the ability to contest or override AI-driven decisions that affect them. The Harvard-based AI Impact on Workers initiative noted concerns around surveillance and privacy when AI is deployed (e.g. monitoring keystrokes or using AI to judge performance)[[56]](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/generative-ai-the-american-worker-and-the-future-of-work/#:~:text=nations%20lack%20the%20urgency%2C%20mental,AI%20and%20avoid%20its%20harms). Over-monitoring can infringe on privacy and create stressful working conditions. Thus, developing ethical guidelines for generative AI use in workplaces is an urgent challenge. Many scholars advocate for frameworks that emphasize transparency (workers know when AI is involved), consent (opting out of AI monitoring), and a “human-in-the-loop” approach for critical judgments. In summary, as generative AI becomes more prevalent in employment decisions and daily work, tackling the bias and ethics challenge is crucial to prevent harm and ensure AI deployment aligns with societal values.

items.quote: he knew his wife, and she conceived and bore [a son]
items.paragraph: Pregnancy and childbirth in the Hebrew Bible are described tersely, often through formulaic phrases like "he knew his wife, and she conceived and bore [a son]" (e.g., Genesis 4:1), focusing less on maternal emotions or physical details and more on divine orchestration and outcomes. Metaphors are tactile and creative: the fetus is knitted like wool (Psalm 139:13; Job 10:11), shaped like clay by a potter (Job 10:9), or curdled like cheese from milk (Job 10:10), growing in the womb's darkness like seeds in earth (Psalm 139:15). Birth involves midwives, crouching positions, and rituals like cord-cutting, washing, salting, and naming, with purity laws for mothers (Leviticus 12). Difficult births are recurrent, symbolizing crisis and uncertainty, as in Eve's promised "pain" (Genesis 3:16), extended to humanity's toil.[bibleodyssey.org](https://www.bibleodyssey.org/articles/pregnancy-and-childbirth-in-the-hebrew-bible/)

items.quote: too good not to have the kind of piano sound they should,
items.paragraph: **Bud Powell and Charlie Parker**: Williams was particularly invested in developing Powell's piano technique and artistic confidence. She believed these young musicians were "too good not to have the kind of piano sound they should," and she worked to help them develop the physical and technical mastery necessary to express their musical innovations. Her mentorship of Parker, who was also part of her circle in mid-1940s New York, reflected her broader commitment to ensuring that bebop's revolutionary harmonic ideas remained grounded in authentic expression.[^22]

items.quote: anime is not just kids’ cartoons
items.paragraph: 4. Common Factors Behind Global Success: Despite their differences, Japanese anime and Nordic Noir share some underlying factors that propelled their worldwide popularity. One key common factor is novelty and differentiation: both offered something fresh and distinct from mainstream American entertainment at the time they gained global traction. For anime, Western audiences of the 1990s–2000s discovered animated works that were unlike Saturday morning cartoons or Disney movies – anime stories could be long-form, serialized, and geared towards teens or adults with complex themes and action. This novelty – “anime is not just kids’ cartoons” – generated intrigue and a passionate fanbase. Likewise, Nordic Noir television emerged in a landscape dominated by English-language crime shows; its foreign-language authenticity (with subtitles), stark cinematography, and slow-burn narrative proved a compelling alternative to slick, formulaic American procedurals. Viewers and critics lauded the authentic gritty realism and strong writing of series like The Killing, which felt novel compared to typical police dramas. Another common success factor is quality of storytelling and production. Both anime and Nordic Noir, at their best, demonstrate high craftsmanship that resonates with audiences. Top-tier anime (e.g. Studio Ghibli films, acclaimed series like Death Note or Attack on Titan) feature sophisticated storytelling, memorable characters, and artistic visuals – elements that transcend language barriers and draw in international fans. Similarly, the best Nordic Noir dramas are meticulously written and acted, with cinematic production values that garnered critical acclaim; for instance, The Bridge and Borgen were praised as on par with the world’s best TV dramas, making them easy for networks like BBC to market globally as prestige content. Fan and community engagement also played a role, especially for anime. Anime’s global spread was significantly enabled by fan communities – early fansubbing groups distributed shows online, anime conventions spread awareness, and a whole generation grew up with anime as part of their identity. This grassroots enthusiasm created a ready market that streaming services later tapped into. Nordic Noir’s spread, while not fan-driven in the same sense, benefited from word-of-mouth among discerning viewers and critics. The buzz around a show like The Killing in the UK (where media coverage and audience curiosity fed off each other) led more broadcasters in other countries to pick up Scandinavian series. Additionally, both leveraged new distribution channels effectively: anime rode the wave of DVD and internet distribution in the 2000s, and Nordic Noir rode the rise of international drama slots on networks (e.g. BBC Four’s Saturday foreign drama slot) and later streaming platforms acquiring foreign content. Another shared factor is that both anime and Nordic Noir had support from their origin countries to reach out – Japan’s industry, along with government’s Cool Japan push, increasingly embraced international licensing (turning what was once piracy-driven distribution into legal streaming), and the Nordic countries, through bodies like the Nordic Council and various film institutes, often supported subtitles, exports, and co-productions to showcase their TV industry abroad[[35]](https://nordics.info/themes/nordic-noir#:~:text=Nordic%20Noir%20has%20both%20contributed,into%20branding%20of%20the%20Nordic). Lastly, both phenomena capitalized on a period (late 2000s/early 2010s) when audiences globally were seeking diverse content. Just as Nordic Noir paved the way for acceptance of non-English TV dramas in the Anglophone world (followed by German, French, Korean series, etc.[[36]](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2016/jan/02/foreign-tv-drama-bbc-channel4-netflix#:~:text=After%20the%20success%20of%20Nordic,Korea%20are%20on%20the%20way)[[26]](https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2016/jan/02/foreign-tv-drama-bbc-channel4-netflix#:~:text=I%20t%E2%80%99s%20not%20only%20Faroese,only%20by%20BBC1%20and%20ITV)), anime’s success prefigured the later ubiquity of international animation and media cross-pollination. In summary, delivering a unique creative product with high quality, exploiting new distribution methods, and fostering a passionate viewership community were common ingredients in the globalization of both Japanese anime and Nordic Noir.

items.quote: a hard taskmistress, demanding and intolerant.
items.paragraph: This critical stance wasn't arbitrary; it reflected her conviction that **music revealed the inner character of the musician**. As one observer noted: Williams expected "great things" of musicians, functioning "in a way, she reminds one of a mother with her children, alternately scolding or praising them, trying to teach them, trying to instill her beliefs in them," yet she was also "a hard taskmistress, demanding and intolerant."[^27]

items.quote: took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the sons of the king who were being murdered, and she put him and his nurse in a bedroom
items.paragraph: Most tellingly, **the story of King Joash and his nurse Jehosheba** reveals the theological significance of nursing relationships for preserving the Davidic line. When the usurper queen Athaliah murders the royal family, Jehosheba (the sister of King Ahaziah) "took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the sons of the king who were being murdered, and she put him and his nurse in a bedroom" (2 Chronicles 22:11). The text emphasizes the role of his nurse in preserving Joash through six years of concealment in the temple: "Joash remained hidden with his nurse at the temple of the LORD for six years while Athaliah ruled the land" (2 Kings 11:3).[^28][^29]

items.quote: On that Day We will ask Hell: 'Are you full?' And it will reply: 'Are there any more?'
items.paragraph: Surah Qaf (Chapter 50) presents one of the most philosophically unsettling depictions of hellfire: "On that Day We will ask Hell: 'Are you full?' And it will reply: 'Are there any more?'" This dialogue personifies hellfire as an active, insatiable force—a living will engaged in consuming souls. The passage operates as a kind of theatrical dialogue, staging an imagined conversation that highlights the infinite hunger of divine punishment and its apparently inexhaustible capacity to encompass more transgressors. The effect is deeply disorienting: hellfire is not merely a location of punishment but an active, sentient force engaged in consumption, and its insatiability becomes metaphorically terrifying.[^27]

items.quote: music with healing in it and spiritual feeling,
items.paragraph: Underlying Mary Lou Williams’s pedagogy was a kind of tough love and deep faith in jazz’s value. She believed young musicians needed heroes and role models from the past: “How can anyone advance without listening to someone older?” she asked, lamenting that modern kids “no longer have heroes – like Babe Ruth” in music[[5]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=music%2C%20and%20a%20new%20pianist%2C,They%27re%20looking)[[17]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=%3E%20%20%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0,Jazz%20has%20healing%20in%20it). Rather than scold or dictate, she felt a master’s inspiring example was key: “Not someone who’s always telling them, ‘Do this, do that,’... but somebody they want to pay attention to”[[17]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=%3E%20%20%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0,Jazz%20has%20healing%20in%20it). Williams happily filled that mentor role. Her students, she said, were “great kids. They’re looking for love, and that’s what’s in the music I’m teaching. Jazz has healing in it, and a lot of love.”[[18]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=%3E%20%20%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0,Arts%2C%20is%20a%20freelance) This almost spiritual view of teaching jazz – as passing on “healing” and “love” – flowed from her own mid-life religious conversion (to Catholicism in 1957) and charity work[[19]](https://folkways.si.edu/artists/mary-lou-williams#:~:text=The%20importance%20of%20the%20blues,technique%20but%20very%20little%20feeling)[[20]](https://angelusnews.com/arts-culture/mary-lou-williams-pioneer-of-sacred-jazz/#:~:text=technique%20but%20very%20little%20feeling). She truly saw jazz as a positive force for the soul. Indeed, Williams often referred to jazz as “music with healing in it and spiritual feeling,” and she worked “in defiance of those who would call jazz ‘the devil’s music’”[[19]](https://folkways.si.edu/artists/mary-lou-williams#:~:text=The%20importance%20of%20the%20blues,technique%20but%20very%20little%20feeling)[[21]](https://angelusnews.com/arts-culture/mary-lou-williams-pioneer-of-sacred-jazz/#:~:text=According%20to%20Father%20Peter%20O%E2%80%99Brien%2C,%E2%80%9D). Whether leading a jazz Mass in a cathedral or a bebop choir in a classroom, her goal was the same: to “open ears” and let people “hear and feel jazz” in its authentic form[[22]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=Mary%20Lou%20and%20the%20bassist,out%20the%20parts%20I%20had). By all accounts, Mary Lou Williams in her final decade became a fervent jazz evangelist, intent on “saving” the music by educating new listeners and players in its rich heritage[[23]](https://music.unc.edu/event/kernodle-pruettlecture24/#:~:text=decades%20that%20followed%20World%20War,movement%20and%20jazz%2C%20her%20work)[[24]](https://music.unc.edu/event/kernodle-pruettlecture24/#:~:text=pianist%2Fcomposer%2Farranger%20Mary%20Lou%20Williams%20during,and%20provide%20another%20means%20for).

items.quote: the most ideal material for skateboards (slides) in theory,
items.paragraph: - Metal-Impregnated Carbon Slides: This technology emerged as an ideal compromise and became the dominant solution for high-performance trains. Composition & Manufacturing: A metal-impregnated carbon slide starts with a porous carbon block (similar to a pure carbon slide), which is then infiltrated with molten metal – typically copper or a copper alloy – under vacuum or pressure. The metal fills the pores and forms a network throughout the carbon, yielding a composite material with both carbon and metal phases. (In effect, this can be seen as a hybrid of the pure carbon and P/M approaches: a graphite matrix with integrated metal.) Advantages: Metal-impregnated carbon combines the best qualities of both earlier types. It retains the self-lubricating, low-friction carbon surface, so contact wire wear remains low (comparable to pure carbon slides)[[41]](https://lttrade.en.made-in-china.com/product/mwdAMOQLhupg/China-Thickness-22mm-Carbon-Contact-Slider-Set-of-Pantograph.html#:~:text=%282%29%20Metal,most%20ideal%20material%20for%20skateboards). At the same time, the infused copper provides high electrical conductivity and higher mechanical strength, approaching that of the P/M slides[[41]](https://lttrade.en.made-in-china.com/product/mwdAMOQLhupg/China-Thickness-22mm-Carbon-Contact-Slider-Set-of-Pantograph.html#:~:text=%282%29%20Metal,most%20ideal%20material%20for%20skateboards). This means lower contact resistance (less heating and arcing) and a sturdier strip less prone to cracking. In short, it offers high strength & low electrical resistance without sacrificing the pantograph–wire interface lubricity – “the most ideal material for skateboards (slides) in theory,” as one source notes[[41]](https://lttrade.en.made-in-china.com/product/mwdAMOQLhupg/China-Thickness-22mm-Carbon-Contact-Slider-Set-of-Pantograph.html#:~:text=%282%29%20Metal,most%20ideal%20material%20for%20skateboards). Disadvantages: The manufacturing process is more complex and costly than for pure carbon (it requires vacuum casting or repeated impregnation cycles to get uniform metal distribution). The strips are heavier than pure carbon and still somewhat softer than pure metal, so they can wear a bit faster than P/M slides – but this is by design to protect the wire. Overall, metal-impregnated carbon has few performance downsides, and any remaining issues (e.g. slight reduction in ultimate strength vs. pure metal, cost) are outweighed by the benefits. Application: This slide type is now the standard for high-speed and high-power railway applications. Nearly all modern high-speed trains (200–350+ km/h) use copper-impregnated carbon strips on their pantographs, as do many modern electric locomotives and high-current commuter trains. For example, China and Europe both use metal-impregnated carbon sliders extensively on their high-speed fleets[[40]](https://lttrade.en.made-in-china.com/product/mwdAMOQLhupg/China-Thickness-22mm-Carbon-Contact-Slider-Set-of-Pantograph.html#:~:text=Where%20the%20pantograph%20of%20electric,by%20the%20first%20two%20skateboards). They are favored for reliable current collection under the demanding conditions of high speed, while minimizing infrastructure wear.

items.quote: Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples

items.quote: started playing commercial rock and what they call ‘free music,’ and all the feeling went out of it.
items.paragraph: Each of those labels reflects a trend that Mary Lou Williams felt did not carry the true spirit of jazz and thus led to a creative dead end. For example, one chopped branch is tagged “Avant Garde” (along with the word “cults” or “black magic”), conveying her low regard for the free jazz/avant-garde movement of the 1960s which, to her, abandoned jazz’s melodic and spiritual foundations[[38]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=left%20and%20looks%20bare%20and,go%20and%20create%20something%20new)[[36]](https://folkways.si.edu/artists/mary-lou-williams#:~:text=the%20evolution%20of%20the%20music%2C,whose%20music%20the%20blues%20flourish). Another broken limb is inscribed “Exercises – Classical Books”, referring to overly technical, academic approaches – practicing scales and European classical methods – which she thought sucked the soul out of jazz playing[[36]](https://folkways.si.edu/artists/mary-lou-williams#:~:text=the%20evolution%20of%20the%20music%2C,whose%20music%20the%20blues%20flourish). And prominently, a barren branch off to one side is labeled “Commercial Rock”, which Williams regarded as a major factor that “endangered and weakened jazz” in the post-bebop era[[37]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=artists.%20,If%20a%20creative). In her view, after the creative peak of bebop, many musicians “started playing commercial rock and what they call ‘free music,’ and all the feeling went out of it.”[[39]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=%3E%20%20%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0,sing%20the%20music%20they%27re%20hearing) Jazz’s forward momentum stalled when it was diluted by rock’s commercialism or by experimental noise without blues feeling. On her tree diagram she even wrote a stark phrase, “creation stopped,” near the point after Bop, signaling that she felt no genuinely new core style emerged after bebop – only offshoots that lacked the vital spirit[[40]](https://iverson.substack.com/p/tt-474-new-from-mary-lou-williams#:~:text=For%20a%20tree%20of%20barren,Jarrett%20to%20be%20dead). Williams summed it up tersely: “We almost lost a great American art” in that period, as those dead branches led jazz “to pot” instead of further growth[[41]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=%3E%20%20%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0,have%20her%20students%20sing%20the).

items.quote: took him up and fled; and it came about that in her hurry to flee, he fell and became lame
items.paragraph: **The account of Mephibosheth's nurse** (2 Samuel 4:4) presents another example of maternal protection of an heir. When news arrives that Saul and Jonathan have been slain, Mephibosheth's nurse "took him up and fled; and it came about that in her hurry to flee, he fell and became lame" (2 Samuel 4:4). Though this account ends in physical disability, the nurse's immediate protective instinct—to flee with the young heir rather than abandon him—demonstrates the wet nurse's role as guardian of dynastic continuity and covenant succession.[^27]

items.quote: The LORD heard his prayer, and his wife Rebekah conceived
items.paragraph: The role of the human father in these narratives is notably circumscribed. Isaac prays for Rebekah; Abraham receives God's promise regarding Sarah; Jacob is present but passive in Rachel's story. The narrative focus privileges divine action and female response rather than paternal initiative. When barrenness is resolved, the text attributes the transformation directly to God's intervention: "The LORD heard his prayer, and his wife Rebekah conceived" (Genesis 25:21). This theological construction subordinates male biological function to divine will, positioning the mother's body as the primary site where God's covenantal purposes are actualized.[^9][^10]

items.quote: I recommend lowering this dose because the patient’s blood pressure has been stable for a month, and their kidney function is declining slightly – suggesting we should be gentler on the kidneys while still controlling blood pressure.
items.paragraph: Narrative justification – e.g. a tailored explanation in natural language. For example, if an AI recommends reducing a patient’s medication dose, it might generate a reasoning statement: “I recommend lowering this dose because the patient’s blood pressure has been stable for a month, and their kidney function is declining slightly – suggesting we should be gentler on the kidneys while still controlling blood pressure.”[[16]](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2508.06352#:~:text=recommendation%20might%20generate%3A%20,while%20maintaining%20good%20pressure%20control). This contrasts with a technical explanation; it reads like how a doctor would justify a decision, incorporating patient history and clinical reasoning.

items.quote: previously often inadequate protection of creative freelancers with irregular incomes
items.paragraph: - Main Program: Germany’s key scheme is the Artists’ Social Insurance Fund (Künstlersozialkasse, KSK), established by the Artists’ Social Insurance Act of 1981/1983[[14]](https://itmedialaw.com/en/what-is-the-ksk-and-what-is-its-aim-what-advantages-are-there-for-artists/#:~:text=statutory%20health%2C%20long,as%20if%20they%20were%20employees). This program brings self-employed artists and publicists into the statutory social security system for health, pension, and long-term care insurance[[15]](https://itmedialaw.com/en/what-is-the-ksk-and-what-is-its-aim-what-advantages-are-there-for-artists/#:~:text=compulsory%20insurance%20with%20a%20statutory,a%20cultural%20policy%20achievement%E2%80%9D%2C%20as). It was specifically designed to address the “previously often inadequate protection of creative freelancers with irregular incomes”[[14]](https://itmedialaw.com/en/what-is-the-ksk-and-what-is-its-aim-what-advantages-are-there-for-artists/#:~:text=statutory%20health%2C%20long,as%20if%20they%20were%20employees).

items.quote: adds something new, with a further purpose or different character, altering the first [work] with new expression, meaning, or message.
items.paragraph: The concept of transformative use has emerged as central to modern fair use analysis, originating from the Supreme Court's decision in Campbell v. Acuff-Rose Music, Inc., involving 2 Live Crew's parody of "Oh Pretty Woman". A transformative work "adds something new, with a further purpose or different character, altering the first [work] with new expression, meaning, or message."[^11]

items.quote: Those who disbelieve in Our signs will We burn with Fire. Each time their skins are burned over, We will replace their skins with new ones so that they may taste the punishment.
items.paragraph: The Qur'anic depiction of bodily transformation in hell, particularly the theme of skins being burned and renewed to perpetuate sensation, functions as extreme theatrical staging of eternal suffering. Qur'an 4:56 describes this phenomenon: "Those who disbelieve in Our signs will We burn with Fire. Each time their skins are burned over, We will replace their skins with new ones so that they may taste the punishment." This description is not merely descriptive but performative—it stages an image of continuous, renewable suffering that assaults the reader's sensory imagination. The detail about renewed skin prevents the imagination from finding comfort in numbness or adaptation; the text insists on perpetual, fresh sensation of pain.[^22]

items.quote: Report on the Construction of Situations
items.paragraph: - Guy Debord, “Report on the Construction of Situations” – defines constructed situations as “the concrete construction of temporary life settings… transformed into a higher, passionate nature”[[9]](https://onscenes.weebly.com/philosophy/towards-a-situationist-international#:~:text=by%20Guy%20Debord).

items.quote: explain the water cycle at a 5th-grade reading level
items.paragraph: - Enhanced Content Creation and Lesson Planning: Generative AI is a powerful aid for creating educational content and materials. Teachers can leverage ChatGPT to brainstorm lesson plan ideas, generate lecture notes or summaries, and produce examples or analogies to explain complex concepts. The AI can also adjust the reading level or style of content, helping tailor materials to different ages and proficiencies. For example, a teacher could ask ChatGPT to “explain the water cycle at a 5th-grade reading level” or to generate an example scenario to illustrate a physics principle. This capability makes lesson preparation more efficient and allows educators to differentiate instruction more easily. Moreover, AI can produce interactive learning resources: ChatGPT can create sample dialogues, role-play scenarios for language practice, or even draft worksheets and case studies. Educators have found that ChatGPT can help design visual aids and presentations as well[[18]](https://www.learningscientists.org/blog/2024/2/15-1#:~:text=Interactive%20Learning%3A%C2%A0With%20the%20assistance%20of,students%20to%20study%20in%20the). By offloading some content creation to AI, teachers can devote more energy to customizing how they deliver that content and engaging directly with students. The end result can be more dynamic and captivating lessons, as AI contributes creative ideas and resources that teachers refine and implement.

items.quote: shape AI’s impact on work and workers
items.paragraph: In conclusion, the literature paints a picture of generative AI as a double-edged sword. The opportunities – greater productivity, new industries, enriched jobs, skill democratization – are exciting and within reach, but realizing them requires navigating the challenges and mitigating the risks discussed earlier. As one Brookings report put it, we face “high stakes for workers” and must be proactive in order to “shape AI’s impact on work and workers” for the better[[52]](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/generative-ai-the-american-worker-and-the-future-of-work/#:~:text=professions.%20,as%20job%20loss%20and%20inequality)[[53]](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/generative-ai-the-american-worker-and-the-future-of-work/#:~:text=Despite%20high%20stakes%20for%20workers%2C,AI%20and%20avoid%20its%20harms). The final table below summarizes several key studies and what they tell us about generative AI’s application in specific industries or occupations, including the positive impacts observed and the risks or limitations noted by researchers.

items.quote: the children struggled together within her
items.paragraph: Rebekah’s pregnancy is described as a harrowing ordeal: “the children struggled together within her” to the point she cries out in distress (Gen. 25:22). The Hebrew term for “struggled” can imply crushing or wrestling, indicating how tumultuous this pregnancy was. When Rebekah consults God, the theological meaning of her difficult childbirth is revealed: “Two nations are in your womb… one people shall be stronger than the other, and the older shall serve the younger” (Gen. 25:23). In other words, her womb contains more than babies – it contains nations in miniature. The twins Jacob and Esau represent Israel and Edom, and their prenatal contention foreshadows the historical struggle between these peoples. The Bible explicitly ties an individual birth to national destiny here. Jacob’s birth gripping Esau’s heel (for which he is named) signifies his supplanting of the firstborn. This birth scene prefigures the later ascendancy of Israel (Jacob) over Edom (Esau). Indeed, scholars note that the motif of twins wrestling in utero recurs to dramatize how two kindred nations will diverge, with the divinely chosen one unexpectedly prevailing[[6]](https://www.thetorah.com/article/why-does-the-torah-describe-babies-born-hands-first#:~:text=,Peretz%29%20will%20be%20dominant). The younger twin’s triumph – contrary to normal primogeniture – becomes a theological statement: Israel’s origin involves God’s election of the unlikely, symbolized by the newborn “grabbing the heel” to overtake the elder[[6]](https://www.thetorah.com/article/why-does-the-torah-describe-babies-born-hands-first#:~:text=,Peretz%29%20will%20be%20dominant).

items.quote: ignore that [anime’s] object consists of moving images
items.paragraph: - Points of Focus Summary: In contrast to the representational approach, which asks “What does this anime mean?”, the media-form approach asks “How does anime work?” and “What are the implications of anime’s form?”. Key points of focus are: visual style and animation technique, narrative form shaped by medium (seriality, genre conventions), production processes and industry context, cross-media integration, and the experiential impact of anime’s audio-visual features. For instance, a media-form scholar might investigate why anime characters have such a broad range of facial stylization and what effect that has on audience empathy – a question rooted in form, not just representation. Lamarre’s critique encapsulates this orientation: he notes that too many analyses “ignore that [anime’s] object consists of moving images” and urges engagement with the specific material qualities of anime as animation[[4]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=,treat%20anime%20as%20text%20in). In practice, this means exploring areas like the use of camera movement in anime, the role of voice acting (seiyū performances) in conveying character, or the impact of digital animation tools on the look of contemporary anime. By focusing on these elements, the media-form approach provides a detailed understanding of anime’s unique language and its place within media arts, complementing the cultural/textual interpretations with insight into how anime creates meaning through form[[8]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=reviews.%20,of%20the%20materiality%20of%20animation)[[7]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=,intertextual%20references%2C%20or%20cute%20characters).

items.quote: use it so you don’t lose it
items.paragraph: - Erosion of Student Skills and Learning Dependency: Over-reliance on generative AI can impede the development of core skills in students. If a student uses ChatGPT to solve every problem or write every essay, they may not practice critical thinking, problem-solving, writing, and creativity – skills that education is meant to foster. Researchers have argued that while ChatGPT can produce work efficiently, it does so in place of the student’s own cognitive effort, potentially leading to a decline in the student’s ability to perform these tasks independently[[26]](https://www.learningscientists.org/blog/2024/2/15-1#:~:text=Ineffective%20development%20of%20core%20skills%3A%C2%A0Due,25). For example, a student who habitually uses AI to generate essay outlines and even content might not develop their ability to construct arguments or communicate in writing. Likewise, having math solutions provided step-by-step could diminish a learner’s perseverance and analytical reasoning practice. If such patterns become ingrained, students’ long-term academic and professional success could be negatively affected[[27]](https://www.learningscientists.org/blog/2024/2/15-1#:~:text=analytical%20and%20decision,25). There is also the risk that students will not learn how to learn – i.e. they might not build the meta-cognitive skills of understanding their own knowledge gaps – since AI gives them immediate answers. In short, “use it so you don’t lose it” applies: educators worry that uncritical use of AI can make students passive recipients of information, hindering the growth of independent thought and creativity.

items.quote: We certainly do not want to use organs from death-row prisoners.
items.paragraph: In his March 2014 Beijing Times interview, Huang stated that death-row prisoners "have the right to donate organs" and that prisoner donations would continue as part of the "voluntary" system once integrated into COTRS. However, when asked directly in 2015 whether organs would still come from death-row prisoners after 2015, Huang replied: "We certainly do not want to use organs from death-row prisoners."[^21][^22]

items.quote: How much more money did the algorithm make?
items.paragraph: Evaluation metrics: The performance of trading models is judged by trading profitability and risk metrics. Studies report cumulative profit or return from back-testing the model’s trading strategy over a test period. Annualized return and Sharpe ratio (return per unit volatility) are standard to evaluate risk-adjusted performance. For strategies, Maximum Drawdown (MDD) is often given to assess downside risk (the largest peak-to-trough portfolio decline)[[44]](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16206v1#:~:text=Portfolio%20optimization%20determines%20the%20optimal,They%20are%20defined%20as). Many papers also measure Precision/Recall of trading signals if the model is framed as predicting buy/sell signals (e.g. precision = fraction of predicted “buy” signals that were profitable). As noted, one LSTM model attained 91.5% directional accuracy in predictions[[57]](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/5/4/101#:~:text=Recent%20studies%20have%20demonstrated%20the,how%20deep%20learning%20can%20process), and an RL agent achieved 92% precision in its trades[[41]](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/5/4/101#:~:text=The%20use%20of%20reinforcement%20learning,where%20trading%20bots%20autonomously%20adapt) – such metrics indicate the model’s predictive quality. In classification terms, Accuracy of predicting up vs down days, and sometimes F1-score if both long and short signals are considered, appear in literature (especially where trading is formulated as a classification problem). However, pure prediction metrics are often supplemented with financial metrics – e.g. “How much more money did the algorithm make?” Thus, it’s common to see Return on Investment (ROI), Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio (which like Sharpe but penalizing only downside volatility) for the strategy[[41]](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/5/4/101#:~:text=The%20use%20of%20reinforcement%20learning,where%20trading%20bots%20autonomously%20adapt). Latency and transaction cost considerations are also evaluated in some algorithmic trading research: for instance, measuring performance net of assumed transaction costs or slippage. In summary, a successful DL-driven trading model in recent research is one that yields higher returns (and Sharpe) than benchmarks (like a buy-and-hold or a moving average strategy) while keeping drawdowns and volatility at acceptable levels – and these outcomes are quantitatively demonstrated with the metrics above[[30]](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/5/4/101#:~:text=Recent%20studies%20have%20demonstrated%20the,trading%20strategies%20in%20real%20time)[[41]](https://www.mdpi.com/2673-2688/5/4/101#:~:text=The%20use%20of%20reinforcement%20learning,where%20trading%20bots%20autonomously%20adapt).

items.quote: not for what it shows, but how it shows it,
items.paragraph: - Media/Formal Analysis (Anime as a Medium): Another major approach treats anime as a distinctive media form and scrutinizes its formal properties, production, and technology. Here the guiding questions are “How does anime as animation work? What are its stylistic and industrial characteristics?” Scholars like Thomas Lamarre spearheaded this by insisting on the “materiality of animation” – examining anime’s visual techniques, image composition, and technologies, rather than only its narrative[[4]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=,treat%20anime%20as%20text%20in). This approach might analyze animation methods (e.g. limited animation, stylized motion, use of layers and effects) or the visual iconography (such as the famous “big eyes” style or techniques for conveying speed/emotion). Researchers in this vein argue that anime studies must engage with anime as animation, not just as illustrated storybooks[[4]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=,treat%20anime%20as%20text%20in)[[8]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=reviews.%20,of%20the%20materiality%20of%20animation). They point out that anime is largely a TV-based medium with specific production constraints and viewing habits, which shape its storytelling. Mitsuyo Wada-Marciano, for instance, highlights that academic discourse tended to privilege a canon of visually complex anime films (like Akira or Ghost in the Shell) while neglecting the mass-produced TV anime series that form anime’s core in Japan[[9]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=studies%2C%20anime%20has%20been%20dislocated,produced%20anime%20TV)[[10]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=around%20canons%2C%20which%20serve%20to,%E2%80%9D). She notes that focusing only on a few artful films (often for their grand themes like cyberpunk or environmentalism) ignores the local, temporal, and technological specificities of most anime – such as how series are made for specific audiences and time-slots, or how they fit into popular culture trends[[9]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=studies%2C%20anime%20has%20been%20dislocated,produced%20anime%20TV)[[10]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=around%20canons%2C%20which%20serve%20to,%E2%80%9D). The media-form approach, therefore, looks at anime’s industry, form, and reception context: production committees, TV broadcasting models, genre conventions, visual and sonic style, etc. It often involves comparing anime to other animation traditions or media forms. By viewing anime “not for what it shows, but how it shows it,” this approach shifts emphasis to anime’s unique language of images and its place in media history[[11]](https://animetudes.com/2020/03/05/defining-anime-part-2/#:~:text=scholars%20chosen%20to%20discard%20an,are%20forever%20blurry%20and%20expanding). In practice, this means scholars might study things like the narrative structures of long-running series, the interplay of manga and anime (adaptation studies), or the transmedia techniques (how anime narratives extend into games, toys, etc.). In summary, the media/formal approach treats anime as an audiovisual medium with its own grammar and production ecosystem, focusing on form, style, and medium-specific context rather than primarily on content message[[4]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=,treat%20anime%20as%20text%20in)[[8]](https://www.animemangastudies.com/2019/01/20/the-shortcomings-and-blind-spots/#:~:text=reviews.%20,of%20the%20materiality%20of%20animation).

items.quote: Sure, you can play like a typewriter [by studying in school], but it’ll make your audience nervous…It’s nothing that’s written down in a book
items.paragraph: In her teaching, Williams placed paramount importance on feeling and the oral tradition of jazz. She believed jazz should be learned by ear and through direct experience rather than solely from books. “Jazz doesn’t come out of school,” she argued – many greats like Dizzy Gillespie and John Coltrane “were playing before they ever studied” formally[[7]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=learned%20them%20in%20about%2015,Then%2C%20in%201942%2C%20she%20moved). Williams felt a purely academic, technical approach produces sterile results: “Sure, you can play like a typewriter [by studying in school], but it’ll make your audience nervous…It’s nothing that’s written down in a book”, she said bluntly[[8]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=%3E%20%20%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0,in%20a%20hook%2C%20you%20know). Instead, she tried to “teach the feeling” of the music[[9]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=have%20to%20hear%20great%20music,semester%2C%20I%20gave%20the%20kids). Her methods were hands-on and immersive: she would “go back to the beginnings of jazz, to spirituals and gospel and the blues,” having students listen and sing along to internalize the sound[[9]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=have%20to%20hear%20great%20music,semester%2C%20I%20gave%20the%20kids). “I have them sing all the eras of jazz,” she explained – for instance, when covering bebop she had the class scat “shoo-be-doo-be-doo” lines[[10]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=going%20back%20to%20the%20beginnings,backward%20and%20did%20all%20the). Only once students “saturate the entire mind” with the sound and feeling of one era would she move on to the next[[11]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=music%20they%27re%20hearing.%20,Pushing%20back%20her). If they lacked the proper feel – as when one class’s blues singing “sounded cold” – Williams would “move backward and do all the spirituals again” until they gained the needed warmth[[12]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=they%20sing%2C%20%60shoo,Pushing%20back%20her). This approach stemmed from her conviction that jazz’s essence is best transmitted “in the ears” and spirit, not just the intellect[[11]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=music%20they%27re%20hearing.%20,Pushing%20back%20her).

items.quote: errors provide us data to improve our predictions
items.paragraph: - Teach “Prediction Awareness” and Flexible Thinking: Educators can help students build an awareness of their own predictions and learn that outcomes can diverge from expectations without disaster. One classroom technique is to openly discuss events after they happen: “What did you expect would occur? And what actually happened? Was it as bad as you feared, or different from what you imagined?” This kind of guided reflection teaches the student that not all predictions will be correct, and that’s okay[[23]](https://www.beyondbridgeseducation.com/blogs/what-mindset-really-is#:~:text=We%20can%20support%20neurodivergent%20learners,by). By labeling surprises and outcomes, the teacher demystifies them – a surprise is no longer a terrifying unknown but an event that can be analyzed and learned from. Over time, the student can internalize that prediction errors are information, not merely threats[[24]](https://www.beyondbridgeseducation.com/blogs/what-mindset-really-is#:~:text=pathways%20as%20you%20rise%20out,of%20the%20pit)[[25]](https://www.beyondbridgeseducation.com/blogs/what-mindset-really-is#:~:text=Mindset%20and%20Neurodivergent%20Brains). For example, if an unexpected fire drill occurs, later the teacher might gently review: “You thought there was a real fire and were very scared. But it turned out to be just a practice – next time, we know that if the alarm rings and the teacher is calm, it’s likely just a drill.” Such debriefs help update the child’s predictive model of the world, making it more accurate and less anxiety-prone. Additionally, explicitly framing mistakes or surprises as learning opportunities (“errors provide us data to improve our predictions”[[24]](https://www.beyondbridgeseducation.com/blogs/what-mindset-really-is#:~:text=pathways%20as%20you%20rise%20out,of%20the%20pit)) can reshape a student’s mindset. They begin to see that if something unexpected happens, they can adapt rather than panic, fostering cognitive flexibility.

items.quote: Then God remembered Rachel, and God heeded her and opened her womb
items.paragraph: The Hebrew Bible establishes a complex understanding of God's role in reproduction that encompasses both immediate divine action and long-term covenant promises. The concept of God "remembering" (zakar) appears frequently in connection with conception, as in the case of Rachel: "Then God remembered Rachel, and God heeded her and opened her womb" (Gen. 30:22) [(31)](https://www.jointhejourney.com/4920-god-is-sovereign-over-the-womb). This remembering represents God's faithfulness to covenant promises rather than simple forgetfulness.

items.quote: an appetite for life, a cosmic rigor and implacable necessity, in the gnostic sense of a living whirlwind that devours the darkness, in the sense of a pain that is necessary and inevitable, of a suffering that is necessary for the continuation and sustenance of life.
items.paragraph: The term "cruelty" in Artaud's formulation does not signify sadistic violence but rather, as Artaud himself explained, "an appetite for life, a cosmic rigor and implacable necessity, in the gnostic sense of a living whirlwind that devours the darkness, in the sense of a pain that is necessary and inevitable, of a suffering that is necessary for the continuation and sustenance of life." Central to Artaud's theory was the principle of "assaulting the senses"—overwhelming spectators through sound, lighting, gesture, and movement to expose them to the base reality of human mortality, fragility, and the precariousness of existence. Artaud sought to force audiences out of passivity into a "poetic state" through visceral confrontation with what he considered fundamental truths about the human condition.[^17][^15]

items.quote: Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you shall be divided; the one shall be stronger than the other, the older shall serve the younger
items.paragraph: The Hebrew Bible presents difficult childbirth as a recurring motif with profound theological and national significance. Rebecca's pregnancy with twins exemplifies this pattern, as the biblical text explicitly states: "The children struggled together within her" (Gen. 25:22), causing her great distress [(65)](https://www.chatholybible.com/resources/bible-verses/people-in-the-bible/rebecca). This struggle is not merely a physical inconvenience but a foreshadowing of the future conflict between the nations that will emerge from her womb. The Lord's response to her distress reveals the cosmic implications of her pregnancy: "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you shall be divided; the one shall be stronger than the other, the older shall serve the younger" (Gen. 25:23) .

items.quote: automatic process we go through when decision making
items.paragraph: - Explicitly Teach Cause-and-Effect and Inference Skills: Some autistic students may benefit from direct instruction in how to use clues and past information to make predictions. This can be done through academic exercises that double as life skills. For example, in reading comprehension lessons, teachers often ask students to predict what will happen next in a story. For an autistic student, this is not just a literacy skill but also a practice in real-world prediction. Teachers can scaffold this by pointing out obvious cues (“The sky turned dark and cloudy in the story – what do you think might happen?”) and guiding the student to form a prediction (“Maybe it will rain”). Connecting these dots explicitly can translate to the student’s daily life (dark clouds mean rain is likely, so they can predict indoor recess). Likewise, science experiments offer a chance to hypothesize (“If we drop two objects, which will hit the ground first?”) and then observe outcomes – a concrete way to see that making guesses and seeing them corrected is a normal process. By training the brain’s prediction muscles in low-stakes contexts, we help the student build confidence and skill in anticipating and updating expectations. This reduces anxiety because the student gradually learns that uncertainty can be approached systematically rather than avoided – they start engaging in the same “automatic process we go through when decision making” but in a more deliberate, practiced manner[[28]](https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7102/13/6/575#:~:text=,making%2C%20and%20modelling%20this).

items.quote: is difficult for customers to anticipate future cloud costs, given the lack of pricing clarity
items.paragraph: Contractual and Financial Barriers: In addition to technical hurdles, cloud providers employ certain contractual terms and pricing structures that make switching costly. One major issue is long-term contracts or volume discounts that incentivize sticking with one provider. For instance, hyperscalers often offer discounted pricing in exchange for multi-year commitments or minimum spend agreements; customers who consider switching would lose these discounts (or even face penalties), creating a disincentive to move. Moreover, cloud pricing models are notoriously complex – business users report difficulty forecasting costs due to myriad service fees and usage-based charges[[24]](https://www.autoritedelaconcurrence.fr/en/press-release/cloud-computing-autorite-de-la-concurrence-issues-its-market-study-competition-cloud#:~:text=The%20presence%20of%20key%20stakeholders,for%20customers%2C%20even%20powerful%20ones). This complexity itself is a barrier: it “is difficult for customers to anticipate future cloud costs, given the lack of pricing clarity”[[24]](https://www.autoritedelaconcurrence.fr/en/press-release/cloud-computing-autorite-de-la-concurrence-issues-its-market-study-competition-cloud#:~:text=The%20presence%20of%20key%20stakeholders,for%20customers%2C%20even%20powerful%20ones), so comparing providers or optimizing across clouds is non-trivial.

items.quote: We almost lost a great American art
items.paragraph: Each of those labels reflects a trend that Mary Lou Williams felt did not carry the true spirit of jazz and thus led to a creative dead end. For example, one chopped branch is tagged “Avant Garde” (along with the word “cults” or “black magic”), conveying her low regard for the free jazz/avant-garde movement of the 1960s which, to her, abandoned jazz’s melodic and spiritual foundations[[38]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=left%20and%20looks%20bare%20and,go%20and%20create%20something%20new)[[36]](https://folkways.si.edu/artists/mary-lou-williams#:~:text=the%20evolution%20of%20the%20music%2C,whose%20music%20the%20blues%20flourish). Another broken limb is inscribed “Exercises – Classical Books”, referring to overly technical, academic approaches – practicing scales and European classical methods – which she thought sucked the soul out of jazz playing[[36]](https://folkways.si.edu/artists/mary-lou-williams#:~:text=the%20evolution%20of%20the%20music%2C,whose%20music%20the%20blues%20flourish). And prominently, a barren branch off to one side is labeled “Commercial Rock”, which Williams regarded as a major factor that “endangered and weakened jazz” in the post-bebop era[[37]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=artists.%20,If%20a%20creative). In her view, after the creative peak of bebop, many musicians “started playing commercial rock and what they call ‘free music,’ and all the feeling went out of it.”[[39]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=%3E%20%20%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0,sing%20the%20music%20they%27re%20hearing) Jazz’s forward momentum stalled when it was diluted by rock’s commercialism or by experimental noise without blues feeling. On her tree diagram she even wrote a stark phrase, “creation stopped,” near the point after Bop, signaling that she felt no genuinely new core style emerged after bebop – only offshoots that lacked the vital spirit[[40]](https://iverson.substack.com/p/tt-474-new-from-mary-lou-williams#:~:text=For%20a%20tree%20of%20barren,Jarrett%20to%20be%20dead). Williams summed it up tersely: “We almost lost a great American art” in that period, as those dead branches led jazz “to pot” instead of further growth[[41]](https://ratical.org/MaryLouWilliams/Mission.html#:~:text=%3E%20%20%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0,have%20her%20students%20sing%20the).

items.quote: Why did the model do that?
items.paragraph: Sources: Transparent AI systems share design/data details openly[[1]](https://www.f5.com/company/blog/crucial-concepts-in-ai-transparency-and-explainability#:~:text=Transparency%20in%20AI%20refers%20to,various%20aspects%20of%20the%20system), while XAI methods provide reasons for specific outputs (answering “Why did the model do that?”)[[13]](https://www.f5.com/company/blog/crucial-concepts-in-ai-transparency-and-explainability#:~:text=Key%20elements%20of%20AI%20explainability,include). However, merely explaining an algorithm’s output is often insufficient for clinical use – hence the push toward more explanatory or reasoning-based AI that delivers context-rich justifications (addressing “Why does this advice make sense here?”)[[4]](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2508.06352#:~:text=While%20XAI%20answers%2C%20,different%20questions%20requiring%20different%20approaches). The example above illustrates the difference: traditional XAI might list abstract feature weights, whereas an AI reasoning approach produces a human-friendly narrative[[17]](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2508.06352#:~:text=Consider%20a%20concrete%20example%20illustrating,recommend%20reducing%20the%20patient%27s%20blood)[[16]](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2508.06352#:~:text=recommendation%20might%20generate%3A%20,while%20maintaining%20good%20pressure%20control).

items.quote: enable the identification of unexpected or high-risk transactions
items.paragraph: Crucially, MindBridge has forged strategic partnerships with major players in the auditing and financial industry, which both bolsters its credibility and expands its reach. Most notably, in April 2023 KPMG International (one of the “Big Four” accounting firms) announced a global strategic alliance with MindBridge[[31]](https://www.mindbridge.ai/company/#:~:text=Named%20a%20Cool%20Vendor%20in,Cool%20Vendors%E2%84%A2%20in%20Finance%20Report). This alliance followed a multi-year collaboration and pilot program with KPMG’s Canadian member firm. Under the partnership, KPMG is integrating MindBridge’s AI technology into KPMG Clara, the firm’s worldwide audit platform. By embedding MindBridge’s advanced statistical, machine learning, and rules-based analytics into KPMG Clara, KPMG auditors gain the ability to analyze client financial transactions at a far more granular level and with greater explainability and risk focus[[32]](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/media/press-releases/2023/04/kpmg-and-mindbridge-announce-alliance-to-power-kpmg-audits-with-ai-technology.html#:~:text=MindBridge%2C%20focused%20on%20harnessing%20the,data%20analytics%20and%20AI%20technology). According to KPMG, incorporating MindBridge’s AI will “enable the identification of unexpected or high-risk transactions” and enhance audit quality across its global engagements[[33]](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/media/press-releases/2023/04/kpmg-and-mindbridge-announce-alliance-to-power-kpmg-audits-with-ai-technology.html#:~:text=KPMG%20and%20MindBridge%20have%20today,to%20provide%20enhanced%20audit%20quality). This is a significant endorsement – KPMG’s use of MindBridge in its core audit process indicates a high degree of trust in the platform and showcases MindBridge as a cutting-edge solution for modernizing audits. The KPMG alliance is being rolled out across KPMG’s international network, training thousands of auditors on using the AI platform[[34]](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/media/press-releases/2023/04/kpmg-and-mindbridge-announce-alliance-to-power-kpmg-audits-with-ai-technology.html#:~:text=Today%E2%80%99s%20announcement%20is%20the%20next,out%20throughout%20the%20global%20network)[[35]](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/media/press-releases/2023/04/kpmg-and-mindbridge-announce-alliance-to-power-kpmg-audits-with-ai-technology.html#:~:text=Image%3A%20Leyton%20Perris). Both KPMG and MindBridge have highlighted that this collaboration is aimed at transforming the audit profession by marrying KPMG’s domain expertise with MindBridge’s AI capabilities, all in a responsible and globally consistent manner[[36]](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/media/press-releases/2023/04/kpmg-and-mindbridge-announce-alliance-to-power-kpmg-audits-with-ai-technology.html#:~:text=modernization%20of%20the%20audit%20industry,led%20auditing%20capabilities)[[37]](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/media/press-releases/2023/04/kpmg-and-mindbridge-announce-alliance-to-power-kpmg-audits-with-ai-technology.html#:~:text=With%20growing%20public%20interest%20on,across%20the%20KPMG%20global%20network).

items.quote: Some of the avant-garde guys think they’re so far out…they’re greater than the other cats – but they’re not,
items.paragraph: She often criticized avant-garde musicians for an attitude of superiority as well. “Some of the avant-garde guys think they’re so far out…they’re greater than the other cats – but they’re not,” she said in one interview, asserting that “all the music is great” if it retains its purpose, but avant-gardists wrongly felt they could ignore everything before them[[60]](https://daveratcliffepiano.com/MaryLouWilliams/MLW-ItsAllGreat-1977.html#:~:text=I%20play%20all%20styles%2C%20everybody,if%20jazz%20doesn%E2%80%99t%20come%20back). Williams took issue with their dismissal of structure: “[They reject] established harmonic and tonal patterns”, which she noted with disapproval[[61]](https://jazztimes.com/features/profiles/mary-lou-williams-cecil-taylor-embraceable-you/#:~:text=Many%20people%20wondered%20why%20Mary,earth%2C%20no%20ears%2C%20not%20even). In her Duke lectures, she did not mince words about these artists, explicitly “attack[ing] others for lacking the spiritual feeling in their music,” a group “primarily comprised of avant-garde musicians”[[62]](https://www.amsmusicology.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/2017-rochester.pdf#:~:text=specifically%20about%20God%20in%20her,I%20suggest%20here%20that). She taught her students that the bop and pre-bop styles were musically and spiritually superior to the avant-garde experimentation that followed[[56]](https://www.amsmusicology.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/2017-rochester.pdf#:~:text=and%20brotherhood%20in%20some%20artists%E2%80%99,her%20general%20beliefs%20on%20spirituality). Williams even visualized this stance on her Jazz Tree by placing “Avant Garde” on a severed branch labeled “Cults & Black Magic,” implying that in her view much of the free jazz scene was like a cultish deviation, spiritually dark and cut off from jazz’s life force[[36]](https://folkways.si.edu/artists/mary-lou-williams#:~:text=the%20evolution%20of%20the%20music%2C,whose%20music%20the%20blues%20flourish).

items.quote: I took him back to Fats Waller – I had him swinging the left hand. He can play anything. And that is the only advice I could give [young players].
items.paragraph: One group of musicians Williams consistently praised were those keeping jazz connected to its sacred and blues roots in new contexts. She applauded, for example, gospel-influenced jazz artists. In her sacred jazz efforts, she found common cause with people like Duke Ellington (who wrote sacred concerts) and probably respected John Coltrane’s spiritually driven approach. She also mentored and encouraged young pianists who showed an eagerness to learn the whole tradition. A great example is Hilton Ruiz, a talented pianist who studied with Williams. She proudly recounted: “I took him back to Fats Waller – I had him swinging the left hand. He can play anything. And that is the only advice I could give [young players].”[[68]](https://daveratcliffepiano.com/MaryLouWilliams/MLW-ItsAllGreat-1977.html#:~:text=I%20have%20a%20lot%20of,advice%20I%20could%20give%20them) Her endorsement of Ruiz (“he can play anything” after learning stride) shows she believed mastering the old styles enabled a musician to handle even the new. She similarly guided other up-and-comers, and her positive evaluations were reserved for those who demonstrated humility and breadth.

items.quote: up to $200,000 for two years
items.paragraph: Cloud Credit Programs: Another pricing-related practice is the extensive use of cloud credits – essentially free or heavily discounted cloud services for certain customers (often startups, developers, or other prospective high-growth clients). On the surface, credits encourage adoption (and indeed can help startups avoid upfront costs[[34]](https://www.autoritedelaconcurrence.fr/en/press-release/cloud-computing-autorite-de-la-concurrence-issues-its-market-study-competition-cloud#:~:text=)). However, competition reports have raised concerns when credit programs are extremely large or selectively targeted in ways that smaller rivals cannot match. The French Competition Authority noted that top providers offer very high-value credits – sometimes “up to $200,000 for two years” – to startups and other strategic customers[[35]](https://www.autoritedelaconcurrence.fr/en/press-release/cloud-computing-autorite-de-la-concurrence-issues-its-market-study-competition-cloud#:~:text=However%2C%20the%20Autorit%C3%A9%20considers%20that,providers%20to%20offer%20them%20profitably). These go far beyond typical free trials in other industries. Such generous credits can act as loyalty-inducing rebates: a startup that builds on (for example) AWS or Azure using free credits may become deeply embedded in that platform’s ecosystem by the time the credits are exhausted. At that point, the cost (and difficulty) to migrate to a different cloud is high, and the customer is effectively “won over” long-term. The French Autorité pointed out that the “vast ecosystem” benefits the big providers, and questioned whether “all cloud providers are able to offer [such credits] profitably”[[35]](https://www.autoritedelaconcurrence.fr/en/press-release/cloud-computing-autorite-de-la-concurrence-issues-its-market-study-competition-cloud#:~:text=However%2C%20the%20Autorit%C3%A9%20considers%20that,providers%20to%20offer%20them%20profitably). The implication is that only the largest players (with deep pockets and broad product monetization) can sustain these large-scale credit incentives, which smaller cloud firms cannot afford – thereby putting smaller competitors at a disadvantage. In competition terms, massive credit programs can be viewed as a form of predatory pricing or fidelity rebate: they lock in future business by offering services below cost initially, in a manner difficult for rivals to counter. Authorities thus advise close scrutiny of targeted cloud credit offers that might foreclose competition over time[[36]](https://www.autoritedelaconcurrence.fr/en/press-release/cloud-computing-autorite-de-la-concurrence-issues-its-market-study-competition-cloud#:~:text=However%2C%20the%20Autorit%C3%A9%20considers%20that,providers%20to%20offer%20them%20profitably).

items.quote: Dragon King = evil feudal lord
items.paragraph: - Ao Bing’s Fate and Dragon King’s Role: Instead of Nezha slaying Ao Guang’s son, Ne Zha 2 begins with Ao Bing already “dead” (after the events of the first film) and Ao Guang launching an attack on Nezha’s home under the mistaken belief that his son is lost. Crucially, Nezha does not kill Ao Bing in this version – on the contrary, he saves Ao Bing’s soul. This removes the original story’s trigger for Nezha’s tragic guilt. Ao Guang, the Dragon King, is still an antagonist at first – he angrily assaults Chentang Pass with his underwater demons – yet his characterization is more nuanced. After a fierce initial battle, Ao Guang agrees to a ceasefire and a test instead of pursuing vengeance at all costs[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ne_Zha_2#:~:text=physical%20bodies%2C%20though%20they%20are,due%20to%20the%20effort%20exerted)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ne_Zha_2#:~:text=Ao%20Guang%20makes%20a%20ceasefire,During%20the%20trials%2C%20candidates). He offers Nezha and Ao Bing a chance to prove themselves (via the three trials) to earn Ao Bing’s resurrection. This portrayal of Ao Guang is a major reversal: in traditional lore he was a vengeful tyrant and an embodiment of the oppressive old guard. In Ne Zha 2, Ao Guang ultimately shows honor and even paternal care. By the film’s climax, Ao Guang switches sides upon realizing the greater threat (he even stands down once Ao Bing is safely restored). The Dragon King is no longer the final villain; in fact, his leadership and “fatherly tenderness” are highlighted[[40]](https://www.chinawriter.com.cn/n1/2025/0206/c404076-40413506.html#:~:text=%E4%BA%BA%E5%BF%83%E4%B8%AD%E7%9A%84%E6%88%90%E8%A7%81%EF%BC%8C%E6%90%BA%E6%89%8B%E5%85%B1%E6%8A%97%E5%91%BD%E8%BF%90%E7%9A%84%E8%BD%AE%E7%9B%98%E3%80%82%E4%B8%8E%E6%AD%A4%E5%90%8C%E6%97%B6%EF%BC%8C%E4%BC%B4%E9%9A%8F%E7%9D%80%E5%93%AA%E5%90%92%E4%B8%8E%E6%95%96%E4%B8%99%E5%AE%8C%E6%88%90%E4%B8%89%E6%AC%A1%E8%80%83%E6%A0%B8%E7%9A%84%E8%BF%87%E7%A8%8B%EF%BC%8C%E7%94%B5%E5%BD%B1%E4%B8%AD%E7%9A%84%E4%BC%97%E5%A4%9A%E6%96%B0%E8%A7%92%E8%89%B2%E4%B9%9F%E7%AB%9E%E7%9B%B8%E9%9C%B2%E9%9D%A2%EF%BC%8C%E6%9C%89%E7%94%B3%E5%85%AC%E8%B1%B9%E7%9A%84%E5%AE%B6%E4%BA%BA%E7%94%B3%E6%AD%A3%E9%81%93%E5%92%8C%E7%94%B3%E5%B0%8F%E8%B1%B9%E3%80%81%E6%89%93%E7%A0%B4%E2%80%9C%E7%99%BD%E5%B9%BC%E7%98%A6%E2%80%9D%E5%AE%A1%E7%BE%8E%E7%9A%84%20%E7%9F%B3%E7%9F%B6%E5%A8%98%E5%A8%98%E3%80%81%E7%88%B1%E6%8A%A4%E7%99%BE%E5%A7%93%E4%B8%94%E4%B8%BA%E4%BA%BA%E7%9C%9F%E6%8C%9A%E7%9A%84%E6%9D%8E%E9%9D%96%E5%A4%AB%E5%A6%87%EF%BC%8C%E6%9B%B4%E6%9C%89%E6%B0%94%E5%AE%87%E8%BD%A9%E6%98%82%E7%9A%84%E5%9B%9B%E6%B5%B7%E9%BE%99%E7%8E%8B%E4%B9%8B%E9%A6%96%E6%95%96%E5%85%89%E2%80%A6%E2%80%A6%E8%BF%99%E4%BA%9B%E4%BA%BA%E7%89%A9%E5%9C%A8%E6%89%93%E7%A0%B4%E5%8E%9F%E6%9C%89%E5%BD%A2%E8%B1%A1%E6%A1%8E%E6%A2%8F%E7%9A%84%E5%90%8C%E6%97%B6%EF%BC%8C%E8%A2%AB%E8%B5%8B%E4%BA%88%E4%BA%86%E5%90%84%E7%A7%8D%E6%9C%89%E8%B6%A3%E7%9A%84%E5%B0%8F%E7%BB%86%E8%8A%82%EF%BC%8C%E5%A6%82%E5%85%B8%E5%9E%8B%E7%9A%84%E2%80%9C%E5%8F%8D%E7%88%B6%E6%9D%83%E5%88%B6%E2%80%9D%E5%BD%A2%E8%B1%A1%E6%95%96%20%E5%85%89%EF%BC%8C%E3%80%8A%E5%93%AA%E5%90%922%E3%80%8B%E4%B8%AD%E7%9A%84%E4%BB%96%E5%A7%8B%E7%BB%88%E4%B8%80%E8%BA%AB%E6%AD%A3%E6%B0%94%E3%80%81%E5%BF%83%E6%80%9D%E7%BB%86%E8%85%BB%E3%80%81%E6%9E%81%E5%85%B7%E9%A2%86%E8%A2%96%E6%B0%94%E8%B4%A8%EF%BC%8C%E5%9C%A8%E9%BE%99%E6%97%8F%E9%9D%A2%E4%B8%B4%E5%8D%B1%E9%99%A9%E6%97%B6%E6%AF%AB%E4%B8%8D%E9%80%80%E8%AE%A9%EF%BC%8C%E9%9D%A2%E5%AF%B9%E5%AD%A9%E5%AD%90%E6%97%B6%E5%8F%88%E8%83%BD%E5%B1%95%E9%9C%B2%E6%9F%94%E6%83%85%EF%BC%8C%E4%BB%8E%E4%B8%8D%E4%BB%A5%E8%80%81%E4%B8%80%E8%BE%88%E7%9A%84%E7%BB%8F%E9%AA%8C%E6%8D%86%E7%BB%91%E4%BB%96%E4%BA%BA%E3%80%82). This undermines the old “Dragon King = evil feudal lord” trope and transforms Ao Guang into a more sympathetic patriarch who can cooperate with the heroes. Essentially, the film shifts blame from the Dragon Tribe to a corrupt Heaven (Wuliang’s sect), reframing the core conflict as not simply Nezha vs. Dragons but heroes (mortal and dragon) vs. injustice.

items.quote: A Cost-Efficient Auto-Scaling Algorithm for Large-Scale Graph Processing
items.paragraph: "A Cost-Efficient Auto-Scaling Algorithm for Large-Scale Graph Processing" proposes a framework combining characteristic-based dynamic repartitioning with smart process monitoring to optimize costs. The approach allocates heterogeneous resources for graph applications through resource-based auto-scaling algorithms that consider graph characteristics. Repartitioning methods adjust graph partitioning across available VMs according to VM types and processing progress, ensuring efficient utilization of heterogeneous resources. Experimental results demonstrate that the cost-efficient provisioning significantly reduces financial costs compared to popular frameworks like Giraph, achieving more than 50% cost reduction while ensuring faster execution through intelligent heterogeneous resource allocation and dynamic repartitioning.[^24]

items.quote: the father of green architecture in PR
items.paragraph: 1st Place – “Mi Casa Resistente” Competition (2018) in Puerto Rico[[28]](https://casaresilientepuertorico.wordpress.com/casas-resilientes-para-puerto-rico/casa-rescate/#:~:text=locales%20de%20una%20casa%20sostenible%2C,primer%20lugar%20de%20dicho%20concurso), a post-hurricane housing challenge.
